grandCruClimats.name: Corton
grandCruClimats.note: One of the named vineyards within the Corton Grand Cru, not a Grand Cru of its own. Its named boundary is for red wine; a white Corton shows the whole Corton area instead.

inao-denom-447.note: Chambertin’s production area takes in Clos de Bèze, whose wine may also be labelled Chambertin - so a Chambertin can come from either.

inao-denom-448.note: Clos de Bèze lies inside Chambertin’s production area, and its wine may also be labelled Chambertin.

inao-denom-477.note: Charmes-Chambertin and Mazoyères-Chambertin share one production area. Mazoyères wine may be labelled Charmes-Chambertin, but not the reverse - so a Charmes can come from either.

inao-denom-809.note: Mazoyères-Chambertin shares its production area with Charmes-Chambertin, and its wine may be labelled Charmes-Chambertin.

inao-denom-361.note: Bonnes-Mares spans Morey-Saint-Denis and Chambolle-Musigny. Its full production area is shown on both village maps; the wine’s designation alone does not identify which side it comes from.

inao-denom-565.note: Échezeaux lies in Flagey-Échezeaux and is a different Grand Cru from Grands-Échezeaux. Its official boundary overlaps a few neighbouring Premier Crus slightly; the map colours that shared ground as Grand Cru.

inao-denom-645.note: Grands-Échezeaux lies in Flagey-Échezeaux. It is a separate Grand Cru from Échezeaux.

inao-denom-1271.note: Les Beaux Monts spans Vosne-Romanée and Flagey-Échezeaux. A small corner of its official boundary overlaps Échezeaux, so this highlight includes ground the map otherwise colours as Grand Cru.

inao-denom-571.note: Clos de la Perrière extends across Fixin and Brochon. Its full production boundary is shown across both communes.

inao-denom-806.note: This overview combines the published Marsannay areas; red and white wines have a smaller production area than rosé. Choose a colour in the selector to explore its boundary. Named village lieux-dits are not mapped individually.

inao-denom-806-red-white.note: This is the published production area for red and white Marsannay. Named village lieux-dits are not mapped individually.

inao-denom-806-rose.note: Marsannay Rosé has a different production boundary from red and white Marsannay. Named village lieux-dits are not mapped individually.

inao-denom-557.note: This appellation spans five communes in two separate parts of the Côte de Nuits. The full production area is shown; the wine name alone does not identify a village or an individual plot.

inao-app-204-village.note: This overview combines the red and white Meursault production areas. Choose a colour to see its own boundary; no single vineyard is identified.

inao-denom-844.note: This is the published white-wine village area for Meursault. Named village lieux-dits are not mapped individually.

inao-denom-2062.note: This is the published red-wine village area for Meursault, also named Meursault Côte de Beaune in the source. Named village lieux-dits are not mapped individually.

inao-denom-2373.note: Meursault Premier Cru Blagny is distinct from the red-wine Blagny appellation. Its published boundary includes several more specific Meursault Premier Crus; selecting any name shows its full production area.

inao-denom-549.note: Corton spans Aloxe-Corton, Ladoix-Serrigny and Pernand-Vergelesses. This is the whole Grand Cru: a Corton without a named vineyard on the label could come from anywhere in it. A few named vineyards, such as Faiveley's Clos des Cortons, have no separate boundary here.

inao-denom-550.note: Corton-Charlemagne is a white-wine Grand Cru spanning all three villages. It overlaps Corton on the map and includes the smaller Charlemagne area, but it is a separate appellation.

inao-denom-476.note: Charlemagne is a separate white-wine Grand Cru in Aloxe-Corton and Pernand-Vergelesses. It lies within the Corton-Charlemagne area but is not the same appellation.

inao-denom-1259.note: Santenots lies in Meursault, but its red wines are sold as Volnay Premier Cru, so a red wine recorded as Meursault Santenots is shown here. This map shows the whole Santenots area; smaller plots such as Santenots du Milieu have no separate Volnay boundary here. Santenots white wines are Meursault Premier Cru, with their own boundaries on the Meursault map.
